written: 2026-10-07, before any product change of this run
rule: Hand labels. `text` is the problem; `chart` is the LLM-style program layout (the program builder in backend/tests/geometry/test_exact_dimensions.py turns it into a program through the production route verify_and_compile). `expect` = served:<exact value> or refused:<stage>[:<reason>]. Served values are checked by oracle.py from the TEXT sizes only (no product import). A chart is an affine layout: its metric meaning is NOT a hypothesis.

charts.axis: A=(0,0,0), B=(b,0,0), C=(0,b,0), S=(b/3,b/3,h) — natural model layout, Euclidean-wrong base
charts.approx: A=(0,0,0), B=(b,0,0), C=(b/2, 0.866·b, 0), S=(b/2, 0.2887·b, h) — decimal approximation of a Euclidean layout
charts.over_vertex: axis chart with S=(0,0,h) — apex drawn over vertex A
charts.N1: the regular-triangular-pyramid-w01 tilted frame A=(k,0,0), B=(0,k,0), C=(0,0,k), S=G+t(1,1,1) (Euclidean-faithful)
charts.flat: axis chart with S=(1,1,0) — apex in the base plane (degenerate chart)
charts.tetra_axis: A=(0,0,0), B=(a,0,0), C=(0,a,0), D=(0,0,a) for tetrahedron ABCD
